title: Security Management Specialists
description: Conduct security assessments for organizations, and design security systems and processes. May specialize in areas such as physical security or the safety of employees and facilities.

tasks.text: Assess the nature and level of physical security threats so that the scope of the problem can be determined.
Respond to emergency situations on an on-call basis.
Recommend improvements in security systems or procedures.
Perform risk analyses so that appropriate countermeasures can be developed.
Inspect physical security design features, installations, or programs to ensure compliance with applicable standards or regulations.
Conduct security audits to identify potential vulnerabilities related to physical security or staff safety.
Design security policies, programs, or practices to ensure adequate security relating to alarm response, access card use, and other security needs.
Test security measures for final acceptance and implement or provide procedures for ongoing monitoring and evaluation of the measures.
Design, implement, or establish requirements for security systems, video surveillance, motion detection, or closed-circuit television systems to ensure proper installation and operation.
Prepare, maintain, or update security procedures, security system drawings, or related documentation.
Prepare documentation for case reports or court proceedings.
Develop conceptual designs of security systems.
Train personnel in security procedures or use of security equipment.
Review design drawings or technical documents for completeness, correctness, or appropriateness.
Provide system design and integration recommendations.
Monitor the work of contractors in the design, construction, and startup phases of security systems.
Budget and schedule security design work.
Inspect fire, intruder detection, or other security systems.
Develop or review specifications for design or construction of security systems.
Interview witnesses or suspects to identify persons responsible for security breaches or to establish losses, pursue prosecutions, or obtain restitution.
Outline system security criteria for pre-bid meetings with clients and companies to ensure comprehensiveness and appropriateness for implementation.
Monitor tapes or digital recordings to identify the source of losses.
Engineer, install, maintain, or repair security systems, programmable logic controls, or other security-related electronic systems.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Operations Analysis
skills.def: Analyzing needs and product requirements to create a design.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Amazon Web Services AWS software, Database software, Microsoft Access, ServiceNow.

skills.name: Operating system software
skills.def: Software to provide the operational interface to a computer and provide higher-level services and APIs. Examples: Linux, Microsoft Windows, UNIX.

skills.name: Development environment software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications which run on a computer or mobile device. Examples: Microsoft Azure software, Microsoft PowerShell.

skills.name: Internet directory services software
skills.def: Software to create or manage the mapping of files, users, or other network resources to unique identifiers. Examples: Microsoft Active Directory, Network directory services software.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.
